title: 「By the time」表示「到……時已經……」
titleEn: Using by the time to show earlier completion

source.file: Sentence Structure 117 -「By the time」表示「到……時已經……」.pdf
omissions: English versions of Chinese-only Important Rules and Benefits headings are faithful editorial translations.

formula: By the time + subject + past simple, subject + had + past participle

formulas.formula: By the time + subject + past simple, subject + had + past participle
Subject + had + past participle + by the time + subject + past simple
By the time + subject + present simple, subject + will have + past participle
Subject + will have + past participle + by the time + subject + present simple

examples.highlight: By the time we received the email, the meeting had already started

rules.zh: By the time 表示「不遲於某個時間點」 這個句型表示一件事情在另一件事情發生之前，或最遲在那個時間點，已經完成。 「買票」先完成，「火車到達」是用來作比較的時間點。
rules.en: By the time means ‘no later than a stated time point’. It shows that one event was completed before another event, or by that point at the latest. Buying the tickets is completed first, while the train’s arrival is the time point used for comparison.
examples: By the time the train arrived, we had bought our tickets.

rules.zh: 描述過去時，通常使用過去完成式 不要寫： 這句容易令人以為電影在莎拉到達的同一刻才開始。
rules.en: For past events, normally use the past perfect for the earlier event. Using the past simple for both events can suggest that the film started at the very moment Sarah arrived rather than earlier.
examples: By the time Sarah arrived, the film had started.

rules.zh: 描述將來時，主句通常使用將來完成式 在 by the time 後面的時間子句中，一般使用現在式，不使用 will。 正確： 錯誤：
rules.en: For future events, normally use the future perfect in the main clause. In the time clause after by the time, use the present simple rather than will.
examples: By the time Sarah arrives, the film will have started.

rules.zh: Already 可以使用，但並非必須 By the time 本身已經帶有「到那時已經」的意思，因此 already 可以加入，也可以省略。 兩句都正確，但加入 already 可以加強「早已完成」的語氣。
rules.en: Already is possible but not compulsory. By the time already conveys ‘by then’, so already may be included or omitted; adding it gives extra emphasis to the fact that the earlier event was completed well before that point.

rules.zh: 句子位置可以前後調動 By the time 子句放在前面時，後面通常加逗號： By the time 子句放在後面時，通常不加逗號：
rules.en: The by the time-clause can come before or after the main clause. When it comes first, it is normally followed by a comma; when it comes last, no comma is normally used.

rules.zh: 否定句和被動句亦可使用 否定句 被動句 與相似句型的分別 By the time 與 When When 只指出某件事情發生的時間。兩件事情可以同時發生，不一定有「較早完成」的意思。 By the time 則強調某件事情在另一個時間點之前已經完成。 簡單而言： ● When：當某件事情發生時 ● By the time：到某件事情發生時，另一件事情已經完成 By the time 與 If If 表示條件。事情可能發生，也可能不發生。 By the time 表示時間先後，而不是條件。 ● If：如果某個條件成立 ● By the time：到某個時間點時，事情已經完成 By the time 與 Once Once 表示一件事情完成後，另一件事情便開始或變得可能，重點放在「接下來發生甚麼」。 By the time 則把某件事情當作時間界線，強調另一件事情在該時間之前已經完成。 ● Once：完成第一件事後，第二件事便發生 ● By the time：到某個時間點時，另一件事已經完成
rules.en: Negative and passive forms can also be used. Do not confuse by the time with when, if or once. When merely identifies when something happens and may describe simultaneous events; by the time stresses that another event was already complete before the stated point. If introduces a condition that may or may not occur; by the time expresses chronological sequence, not a condition. Once focuses on what begins or becomes possible after a first event is completed; by the time treats one event as a deadline or boundary and emphasizes that another event was completed before it.
examples: By the time：到某件事情發生時，另一件事情已經完成
By the time：到某個時間點時，事情已經完成
Once：完成第一件事後，第二件事便發生
By the time：到某個時間點時，另一件事已經完成
By the time the deadline arrived, we had not finished the report.
By the time we opened the website, all the tickets had been sold.
When pressure rises, good leaders speak more carefully.
By the time the leader spoke, the pressure had already risen.
If you ignore early warnings, small problems become expensive mistakes.
By the time the company noticed the problem, it had become an expensive mistake.
Once you understand the pattern, it becomes easier.
By the time you finish this exercise, you will have understood the pattern.

benefits.zh: 清楚交代事情的先後次序 這個句型讓讀者立即知道哪件事情較早完成，以及哪件事情是之後的時間點。 第二句更清楚地把「收到電郵」設定為時間點，並強調會議在那之前已經開始。
benefits.en: It makes the sequence of events clear. Readers can immediately tell which event was completed earlier and which later event serves as the time point. In the comparison, the second sentence more clearly makes receipt of the email the reference point and emphasizes that the meeting had already begun.

benefits.zh: 方便描述截止時間和進度 你可以使用這個句型說明一項工作會在某個期限或事件之前完成。 這對學校計劃、工作進度、行程安排和未來目標特別有用。
benefits.en: It helps describe deadlines and progress. You can use the structure to say that work will be completed before a deadline or another event. It is especially useful for school plans, work progress, itineraries and future goals.
examples: By the time the manager returns, we will have finished the report.

benefits.zh: 幫助讀者掌握故事時間線 在故事、新聞報道或經歷描述中，幾件事情可能在不同時間發生。By the time 可以把兩個時間點 清楚連接起來，避免讀者混淆。
benefits.en: It helps readers follow a story timeline. In stories, news reports or accounts of experience, events may occur at different times; by the time links two time points clearly and prevents confusion.

benefits.zh: 把兩項時間資料合併成一句 你不需要把事情分成兩個短句。 使用 By the time 後，兩項資料之間的關係更加清楚。
benefits.en: It combines two pieces of time information in one sentence. You do not need to split the events into two short sentences, and by the time makes their relationship clearer.

benefits.zh: 避免過度使用 When 和 Before 這個句型提供另一種自然的時間表達方法，令寫作和說話不會不斷重複 when 或 before。
benefits.en: It avoids overusing when and before by providing another natural way to express time relationships in speech and writing.

benefits.zh: 幫助你自然運用完成式 By the time 經常與過去完成式和將來完成式一起使用。掌握這個句型後，你會更容易表達「在某 個時間之前已經完成」的意思。
benefits.en: It helps you use perfect tenses naturally. By the time often occurs with the past perfect and future perfect, so mastering it makes it easier to express that something was or will be completed before a particular time.
